title: Chemical table
statementMd:
Innopolis University scientists continue to investigate the periodic table. There are $*n*·*m*$ known elements and they form a periodic table: a rectangle with $*n*$ rows and $*m*$ columns. Each element can be described by its coordinates $(*r*, *c*)$ ($1 ≤ *r* ≤ *n*$, $1 ≤ *c* ≤ *m*$) in the table.

Recently scientists discovered that for every four different elements in this table that form a rectangle with sides parallel to the sides of the table, if they have samples of three of the four elements, they can produce a sample of the fourth element using nuclear fusion. So if we have elements in positions $(*r*_{1}, *c*_{1})$, $(*r*_{1}, *c*_{2})$, $(*r*_{2}, *c*_{1})$, where $*r*_{1} ≠ *r*_{2}$ and $*c*_{1} ≠ *c*_{2}$, then we can produce element $(*r*_{2}, *c*_{2})$.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2aad7759be953a55c88f692b50d56d7eeaf2b106.png)

Samples used in fusion are not wasted and can be used again in future fusions. Newly crafted elements also can be used in future fusions.

Innopolis University scientists already have samples of $*q*$ elements. They want to obtain samples of all $*n*·*m*$ elements. To achieve that, they will purchase some samples from other laboratories and then produce all remaining elements using an arbitrary number of nuclear fusions in some order. Help them to find the minimal number of elements they need to purchase.

## Input

The first line contains three integers $*n*$, $*m*$, $*q*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 200 000$; $0 ≤ *q* ≤ *min*(*n*·*m*, 200 000)$), the chemical table dimensions and the number of elements scientists already have.

The following $*q*$ lines contain two integers $*r*_{*i*}$, $*c*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $1 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ *m*$), each describes an element that scientists already have. All elements in the input are different.

## Output

Print the minimal number of elements to be purchased.

## Note

For each example you have a picture which illustrates it.

The first picture for each example describes the initial set of element samples available. Black crosses represent elements available in the lab initially.

The second picture describes how remaining samples can be obtained. Red dashed circles denote elements that should be purchased from other labs (the optimal solution should minimize the number of red circles). Blue dashed circles are elements that can be produced with nuclear fusion. They are numbered in order in which they can be produced.

**Test 1**

We can use nuclear fusion and get the element from three other samples, so we don't need to purchase anything.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c8701a0ca816e4bb28875e067ada59e6076373c7.png)

**Test 2**

We cannot use any nuclear fusion at all as there is only one row, so we have to purchase all missing elements.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/73d199cd86524d99bd88645930f0a1950eeafcd7.png)

**Test 3**

There are several possible solutions. One of them is illustrated below.

Note that after purchasing one element marked as red it's still not possible to immidiately produce the middle element in the bottom row (marked as 4). So we produce the element in the left-top corner first (marked as 1), and then use it in future fusions.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8ac8b349fe9055dacd4232180d8e40af55547770.png)
statementZhMd:
Innopolis 大学的科学家们继续研究元素周期表。已知有 $*n*·*m*$ 种元素，它们组成一个元素周期表：一个有 $*n*$ 行和 $*m*$ 列的矩形。每种元素都可以用它在表中的坐标 $(*r*, *c*)$（$1 ≤ *r* ≤ *n*$，$1 ≤ *c* ≤ *m*$）来描述。

最近，科学家们发现，对于表中任意四种不同的元素，如果它们组成一个边与表的边平行的矩形，那么只要拥有其中三种元素的样本，就可以通过核聚变制造出第四种元素的样本。因此，如果我们拥有位置为 $(*r*_{1}, *c*_{1})$、$(*r*_{1}, *c*_{2})$、$(*r*_{2}, *c*_{1})$ 的元素样本，其中 $*r*_{1} ≠ *r*_{2}$ 且 $*c*_{1} ≠ *c*_{2}$，那么我们就可以制造出元素 $(*r*_{2}, *c*_{2})$。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2aad7759be953a55c88f692b50d56d7eeaf2b106.png)

核聚变中使用的样本不会被消耗，并且可以在之后的核聚变中再次使用。新制造出的元素也可以用于之后的核聚变。

Innopolis 大学的科学家们已经拥有 $*q*$ 种元素的样本。他们希望获得全部 $*n*·*m*$ 种元素的样本。为此，他们会从其他实验室购买一些样本，然后按照任意顺序进行任意次核聚变，以制造出所有剩余的元素。请帮助他们求出需要购买的元素样本的最少数量。

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$、$*q*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 200 000$；$0 ≤ *q* ≤ *min*(*n*·*m*, 200 000)$），分别表示化学表的行数、列数以及科学家们已经拥有的元素数量。

接下来的 $*q*$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $*r*_{*i}$、$*c*_{*i}$（$1 ≤ *r*_{*i} ≤ *n*$，$1 ≤ *c*_{*i} ≤ *m*$），表示科学家们已经拥有的一种元素。输入中的所有元素均不相同。

## 输出格式

输出需要购买的元素样本的最少数量。

## 说明

对于每个样例，都配有一张用于说明的图片。

每个样例的第一张图片描述了初始可用的元素样本集合。黑色十字表示实验室最初拥有的元素。

第二张图片描述了如何获得剩余的样本。红色虚线圆表示应从其他实验室购买的元素（最优方案应使红色圆的数量最少）。蓝色虚线圆表示可以通过核聚变制造的元素。它们按照制造顺序编号。

**测试 1**

我们可以利用其他三个样本进行核聚变，从而获得该元素，因此不需要购买任何东西。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c8701a0ca816e4bb28875e067ada59e6076373c7.png)

**测试 2**

由于只有一行，我们完全无法进行核聚变，因此必须购买所有缺失的元素。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/73d199cd86524d99bd88645930f0a1950eeafcd7.png)

**测试 3**

有多种可行方案。其中一种如下图所示。

请注意，购买一个标记为红色的元素后，仍然无法立即制造出底行中间的元素（标记为 4）。因此，我们先制造左上角的元素（标记为 1），然后在之后的核聚变中使用它。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8ac8b349fe9055dacd4232180d8e40af55547770.png)
